title: SOC2 ↔ ISO control translation — 1:1 dry-run scratchpad
content:
Purpose / context:
- Prep notes for 1:1 with Alex before auditor dry-run (external audit team scheduled in 3 weeks).
- Goal: confirm control owners, evidence locations, and call script that maps SOC2 CC controls to ISO clauses so we don't fumble translations.
- Keep this messy — checklist + phrases I can read verbatim during the dry-run.

High-level agenda for 1:1 (15–20m):
1) Quick readout: where we are (GAP summary). 2) Walk control mapping for the 8 controls flagged as higher-risk. 3) Agree owners + evidence links. 4) Decide dry-run script + escalation path.

What I want from Alex:
- Buy-in on proposed owner changes for CC6 (change management) and CC7 (logical access).
- Approval on using the packaged KMS docs as primary evidence for CC3 (confidentiality).
- Clarity on which vendor risk exceptions we can carry forward and which need mitigation before auditor arrival.

Quick gap snapshot (top items to speak to):
- CC6 (Change mgmt): missing formal rollback evidence for two infra rollouts (2025-07, 2025-09). Proposed: ask release-eng to produce postmortem + rollback runbook. Owner: Devon. ETA: 2026-02-28.
- CC7 (Logical access): temporary contractors in SSO audit log flagged; need attestation from Hiring/People Ops for contractual access end dates. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-02-24.
- CC3 (Confidentiality/encryption): KMS rotation procedure written but not in Confluence section expected by auditor. Action: move docs -> confluence/crypto and attach key rotation logs from S3. Owner: Paulina (me) + infra. ETA: 2026-02-21.
- Vendor risk: two vendors (third-party observability, external model hosting) have incomplete questionnaires. We have compensating controls but need final sign-off. Owner: Alex to escalate to procurement. ETA: 2026-03-05.

Control translation notes (short mapping phrases to say aloud):
- "SOC2 CC3 maps to ISO A.8/A.10/A.13 territory — highlight our KMS + network segmentation as the primary artifacts."
- "CC6 change control: correlate ISO A.12 change management records with our Jira release tags + rollout policies in the release playbook."
- "CC7 logical access: show SSO audit export + RBAC matrix; link to employee offboarding checklist and artifact in HR."

Evidence checklist (short form) — call these out, confirm link and owner in 1:1:
- KMS key rotation logs — owner: Infra (Devon). Location: S3 /confluence link. Format: CSV + screenshot. Status: partial.
- SSO audit export (last 12 months) + RBAC matrix — owner: Identity (Maya). Location: internal vault link. Status: missing contractor attestation.
- Release postmortems for Jul/Sep infra rollouts — owner: Release Eng (Devon). Location: Jira SEC-2345 sub-tasks. Status: missing rollback runbook.
- Vendor questionnaires (observability + model host) — owner: Procurement (Alex). Location: procurement drive. Status: incomplete.
- Encryption architecture diagram + network segmentation — owner: Infra (Paulina + Devon). Location: confluence/arch. Status: draft, needs tidy.

Questions to confirm with Alex (concrete ask lines):
- "Can procurement expedite the outstanding vendor questionnaires and add an attestation field for data-handling?"
- "For the contractor SSO issue: is an HR attestation acceptable as evidence or do we need signed termination records?"
- "Do we want to surface KMS rotation logs directly in Confluence or keep them in S3 with a signed pointer? Which is auditor-friendly?"

Dry-run script / phrases for the auditor call (keeps me on track):
- Intro: "Hi — I'm Paulina, security ops. For this control area we will show the mapping between Redwood's operational practices and the SOC2 criteria; we can also crosswalk to ISO clauses where helpful."
- For change mgmt: "We use Jira for change requests, tagged release pipelines for deployment, and a post-deploy verification checklist. Here's a sample ticket + the deployment tag that rolled the change into production."
- For access control: "SSO centralizes access; offboarding is automated with HR triggers. Shared here is the last 12 months of SSO logs plus the RBAC matrix."
- For KMS/encryption: "Encryption is enforced at rest and in transit; our key rotation schedule and cloud KMS configuration are attached. We can provide logs for the last two rotations."

Potential small talk / placemats (notes to self):
- Mention how Private deployments use customer-managed keys (good to show flexibility).
- Emphasize rollout fallback policies (reduces concern about missing rollback runbook).
- If auditor pushes on vendor incomplete questionnaires, propose compensating control: contractual right-to-audit clause + perimeter isolation evidence.

Follow-up action items (concrete, assignable):
- Paulina: Copy KMS rotation logs into confluence/crypto + add readme linking to S3 snapshot. Due 2026-02-21.
- Devon: Produce rollback runbook and attach to the two postmortems (Jul/Sep). Due 2026-02-28.
- Maya: Get contractor access attestation from People Ops (signed). Due 2026-02-24.
- Alex: Escalate vendor questionnaires to procurement and confirm remediation plan. Due 2026-03-05.
- Paulina + Alex: Draft 10-min dry-run script and rehearse 1:1 (schedule 30m). Suggested time: week of 2026-02-22.

Notes re: evidence formats auditor prefers (from last year's notes):
- Prefer consolidated PDFs with a short executive summary rather than raw CSVs. I'll generate 2–3 "executive evidence packets" for each control.
- Annotated screenshots with timestamps help; I'll add brief annotations showing search filters used.

Risk statements to have ready (short):
- If vendor questionnaires remain open, residual risk = medium (limited access to vendor personnel). Compensating control: network ACLs + data minimization.
- Missing rollback runbook increases incident recovery time; mitigated by automated canary rollouts currently in place.

Reminder: things I can't promise in 1:1 (call-outs to avoid):
- Don't commit to rewriting the entire network diagram — propose incremental edits and a designated reviewer.
- Don't promise vendor remediation timelines beyond procurement's scope.

Quick template email to send after 1:1 (to paste into Slack/email):
"Alex / team — thanks for the run-through. Per our discussion, I'm going to: 1) add KMS logs to confluence, 2) create the rollback runbook PR, 3) collect contractor attestations. Please confirm when procurement has updated the vendor questionnaires. I'll circulate the dry-run script once it's ready"

Stuff to log in Jira after 1:1 (immediate tickets):
- SEC-XXXX: Add KMS evidence to Confluence (link). -> Paulina.
- SEC-XXXX: Rollback runbook for Jul/Sep rollouts -> Devon.
- SEC-XXXX: Contractor access attestation -> Maya.

Open questions I still have (to research before 1:1):
- Does the auditor accept HR attestations as primary evidence for contractor offboarding? (check past audit notes)
- Exact retention window preference for KMS logs (12 vs 24 months).
- Which Confluence space auditors prefer — security vs infra?

Endnotes (personal):
- Keep script short and repeat the mapping line: "here's the policy, here's the artifact, here's the timestamped evidence."
- Bring printed evidence packets to the audit interview — auditors sometimes like physical PDFs.

-- Paulina
(scratchpad: will clean into a confluence short checklist once items nailed down)
